promptText: What project management tools exist for a startup founder working solo?
rawText:
As a solo startup founder, your biggest enemy is **context switching** and **tool overhead**. You need a tool that requires minimal maintenance so you spend time *building and selling*, not managing your project management tool.

Here is a breakdown of the best project management tools for solo founders, categorized by how you work.

---

### 1. The "All-in-One" Business Hubs
*Best if you want your tasks, meeting notes, CRM, and product roadmap in one single place.*

*   **Notion**
    *   **Why it’s great for solo founders:** Notion isn't just a task manager; it's a second brain. You can manage your code roadmap, draft investor updates, maintain a light CRM for early customers, and track daily tasks in one tab.
    *   **Best for:** Founders who want flexibility and a single source of truth for their entire business.
    *   **Pricing:** Free tier is very generous; Paid plan starts at $8–$10/month.
    *   *Warning:* It is easy to spend hours building "pretty" dashboards instead of actual work. Stick to simple templates.
*   **Coda**
    *   **Why it’s great:** Similar to Notion, but with much stronger data automation, formulas, and interactive docs. 
    *   **Best for:** Founders who love data, spreadsheets, and automated workflows without writing code.

---

### 2. The Software & Technical Founder Standard
*Best if you are building a SaaS or tech product and want speed.*

*   **Linear**
    *   **Why it’s great for solo founders:** Linear is ridiculously fast, keyboard-driven, and beautifully designed. It cuts out all the enterprise clutter of Jira. It handles issue tracking, cycles (sprints), and roadmaps effortlessly.
    *   **Best for:** Developer-founders building software who want to ship fast.
    *   **Pricing:** Free for up to 250 active issues (plenty for a solo founder).
*   **GitHub Projects**
    *   **Why it’s great:** If your code is already on GitHub, using GitHub Projects eliminates context switching entirely. You can link tasks directly to Pull Requests and commits.
    *   **Best for:** Pure developer founders who want zero friction between task management and code.
    *   **Pricing:** 100% Free.

---

### 3. AI & Calendar-Integrated Tools
*Best if you struggle with time management, calendar blocking, and prioritization.*

*   **Motion (UseMotion)**
    *   **Why it’s great for solo founders:** As a solo founder, you wear 10 hats. Motion uses AI to automatically build your daily schedule. You input your tasks, deadlines, and estimated time, and Motion inserts them directly into your calendar around your meetings. If a task slips, it automatically reschedules your day.
    *   **Best for:** Founders overwhelmed by *when* to do their work.
    *   **Pricing:** Premium tool (approx. $19–$34/month), but often worth it for the time saved.
*   **Sunsama**
    *   **Why it’s great:** A "calm" daily planner. It pulls tasks from Notion, GitHub, Trello, and your email into a single daily drag-and-drop schedule. It prevents burnout by warning you when you've planned too much work in a single day.
    *   **Best for:** Founders struggling with work-life balance and focus.

---

### 4. Simple, Fast, and Frictionless
*Best if you just want to write things down and check them off.*

*   **Todoist**
    *   **Why it’s great:** Unmatched Natural Language Processing (you can type "Pitch Deck draft next Tuesday at 3pm #Marketing" and it sets everything automatically). It’s blazingly fast on phone and desktop.
    *   **Best for:** Non-technical founders who want low friction and execution-focused task tracking.
    *   **Pricing:** Free tier is great; Pro is $4/month.
*   **Trello**
    *   **Why it’s great:** The classic digital Kanban board. Drag cards from "To Do" to "In Progress" to "Done." Zero learning curve.
    *   **Best for:** Visual thinkers who want a lightweight setup.

---

### Recommendations by Founder Type

| If you are a... | Go with... | Why? |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Technical / Developer Founder** | **Linear** or **GitHub Projects** | Blazing fast, built for shipping code, no bloat. |
| **Generalist / Non-tech Founder** | **Notion** | Keeps your docs, strategy, CRM, and tasks in one place. |
| **Overwhelmed / Bad at Time Mgmt** | **Motion** | AI plans your day so you don't have to think about what's next. |
| **Minimalist / Execution-focused** | **Todoist** | Quickest way to get tasks out of your head and onto paper. |

---

### Tools Solo Founders Should Avoid (For Now)
*   **Jira / Azure DevOps:** Over-engineered for enterprise teams; setup time will waste hours.
*   **ClickUp:** Feature-rich, but often too slow, complex, and overwhelming for a single user.
*   **Asana / Monday.com:** Great for teams of 10+, but expensive and unnecessary for a solo builder.

### The #1 Rule for Solo Founders
**Do not spend more than 1 hour setting up your system.** Pick one tool, build a 3-column board (*To Do, In Progress, Done*), and start working on your core business.
